english.title: Proceeds of Crime Act - tipping off - money launder
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing or suspecting that a disclosure falling within

(A)_[section 337]_
(B)_[section 338]_

of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 had been made, you made a disclosure which was likely to prejudice any investigation which might be conducted following that disclosure
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 333 and 334 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording is now OBSOLETE - repealed by Para 3 of Sch 2 to the Terrorism Act 2000 and Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (Amendment) Regulations 2007- S.I. 2007/3398 refers. New offences relating to "tipping off" were inserted by Schedule 1 of these regulations and are contained in section 333A of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002.
They may be viewed at Standard Offence Wordings H9230 and H9231, the appropriate CJS Codes are:- PC02024 and PC02025 respectively.

(i) See section 332(6) for circumstances in which a person does not commit this offence.
(ii) See section 332(5) for an explanation of the term "required disclosure". MoPI group cannot be established from the offence code alone. Group 2 or 3 may apply depending on the nature of the related crimes. Manual MoPI review is required.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
